claim: The one-word look that sets the entire colour stack, so the same frame can read as a warm memory, a cold procedural or a horror beat without a single subject tag changing. It is the first knob a director turns because it re-scores the emotion of footage that is already shot.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: warm colors, orange tint, golden tone
cool colors, blue tint, cold color palette
teal and orange, cyan shadows, orange highlights, complementary colors
bleach bypass, desaturated, high contrast, silver tone
high key, bright, low contrast, washed out
low key, dark, deep shadows, high contrast
faded colors, muted color, lifted blacks, low saturation
blue theme, deep blue shadows, cool tint
sodium vapor light, amber tint, yellow theme, monochromatic orange
pastel colors, soft colors, low contrast
vivid colors, saturated colors, colorful, high saturation
green theme, sickly green tint, desaturated green

review.issue: cool_film ("cool colors, blue tint, cold color palette") and night_blue ("blue theme, deep blue shadows, cool tint") are the same instruction to the model expressed twice; with a floodlit night stadium as the fixed subject both will also sit close to the ungraded baseline, so the pair reads as a render glitch rather than two looks.
review.fix: Give night_blue a value component the other lacks — "blue theme, night, dark, deep blue shadows" — so one panel is a hue shift and the other is a hue shift plus a darkening, or fold the two values together.
